programme.title: London South East Main
programme.desc: It's a battle for the main course for three of London and the South East's finest chefs - Matt Gillan, Lee Westcott and Mark Froydenlund. Returning contender Matt is determined to bring home a 10 with his ambitious celebration of the billy goat but has he bitten off more than he can chew?

programme.title: London South East Dessert
programme.desc: It's dessert day and the London and South East chefs are striving to secure one of the two spots in tomorrow's Regional Final. The scores are close, so it's all to play for, as today marks the end of the competition for one man.

programme.title: London South East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London and South East chefs are cooking all four courses again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by Mary Gwynn, author of the official WI centenary cookbook. Together they'll decide which chef goes through to represent the region in the National Finals.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Three of the Central Region's finest chefs - Pip Lacey, Richard Bainbridge and Jason Hodnett - attempt to impress this week's veteran judge with their starters. With big boots to fill, Angela Hartnett's protégé Pip is the only newcomer in the kitchen. Will she beat the boys to claim victory?

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: The three Central Region chefs - newcomer Pip Lacey, 4th time competitor Richard Bainbridge and returning chef Jason Hodnett - fight it out in the fish course. Pip is hoping to outclass her rivals with a smoked haddock dish inspired by her Grandma.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: It's a battle for the main course with three Central Region chefs - Pip Lacey, Richard Bainbridge and Jason Hodnett. Once again Jason is taking risks with his unusual collection of ingredients.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: It's the last chance for the Central Region chefs to impress, with the dessert course. Only two chefs can go through to cook for the judges so with everything to play for, who will plate up perfection and who will be sent packing?

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Central Region chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They'll be joined by former chair of the Women's Institute Helen Carey, who will help decide who will have the glory of representing the region in the National Finals.

programme.title: Finals Week: Starter
programme.desc: It's the starter course, and eight of the finest chefs in the country are battling it out to plate up impeccable dishes worthy of the Women's Institute. The judges are joined by WI Calendar Girl Angela Baker, but after Oliver reveals that this year it will be much tougher to make it onto the judge's shortlist, who will keep their cool and secure a place?

programme.title: Finals Week: Fish
programme.desc: It's the battle for the fish course. Those who failed to make it to the shortlist with their starters are hoping to do better. The judges are joined by Kristy Bowen, who knows the impeccable standards the WI will expect.

programme.title: Finals Week: Main
programme.desc: It's main course day, the half-way point in Finals Week, and those chefs who have yet to get a dish on the shortlist are feeling the heat. With only dishes judged to be perfect in with a chance at reaching the WI banquet, the standards are higher than ever before.

programme.title: Finals Week: Dessert
programme.desc: It's the last chance for the eight regional champions to get a dish in contention for the final banquet. Those who failed to make it to the shortlist are going all out. The judges are joined by Mary Gwynn, the author of the WI centenary cookbook.

programme.title: Finals Week: Banquet
programme.desc: The banquet is finally here. It's the culmination of months of hard work as the winning chefs strive to plate up perfect dishes for the Women's Institute ladies at London's historic Draper's Hall.

programme.title: Scotland Starter
programme.desc: Three top chefs from Scotland are out to impress this week's veteran judge and be crowned Scottish champion. Adam Handling has already won a number of industry awards and is full of confidence. His starter sets out to take the diner on a tour of the UK's best producers. He's up against Michael Bremner, who is hoping to impress with contemporary ingredients including Birch sap and Douglas fir oil. Ally McGrath is celebrating his nation's finest produce and making his very own version of haggis.

programme.title: Scotland Fish
programme.desc: Three newcomers to the competition create their fish dishes in a bid to be crowned Scottish champion. The standard is so high the veteran judge is moved to tears.

programme.title: Scotland Main
programme.desc: Ally McGrath has been keeping the veteran judge entertained with his very individual approach. Also, the highly competitive Adam Handling has been showcasing the finest produce grown and caught in and around the UK in his menu. Once again Michael Bremner is out to show how inventive he can be.

programme.title: Scotland Dessert
programme.desc: One chef will go home, and today the veteran judge finds himself with a difficult decision to make. Inventive chef Michael Bremner is recreating the Scottish desserts of his childhood, Adam Handling is sticking with his trademark Asian flavours and Ally McGrath is tempering chocolate for the very first time.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: Scotland's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for the judges for the very first time. Both chefs have decided to make changes to some of their dishes, taking on board criticisms made during the week by the veteran judge.

programme.title: South West Starter
programme.desc: Chef Josh Eggleton is back for a third time. Last year he made the national finals when his starter was shortlisted for the banquet, this year he intends to go one step further and cook at the banquet. One of his rivals last time, Jude Kereama is also back and out to do better than he did previously. The third competitor is newcomer Chris Wheeler who is originally from Swanage in Dorset.

programme.title: South West Fish
programme.desc: There are some exciting dishes on the menu as the three chefs from the South West tackle the fish course. Chef Josh Eggleton is hoping to impress with an original take on Bolognese, just one of six elements on his complex fish dish.

programme.title: South West Main
programme.desc: It is the main course and chef Chris Wheeler is out to show just how theatrical he can be, and his ideas are surprising everyone in the kitchen. No one knows quite what to expect, and the veteran chef is hoping it tastes as good as it looks.

programme.title: South West Dessert
programme.desc: It is the dessert course, and it is Josh Eggleton who has come up with the most ambitious dessert. He is creating his own self-serve ice cream made from vegetables, and making everything from scratch including toppings and syrups.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the South West region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. They are joined by guest judge, journalist and restaurant critic, Grace Dent.

programme.title: North West Starter
programme.desc: Two newcomers to the competition are challenging reigning North West champion Matt Worswick. Adam Reid is head chef at Manchester's Midland hotel and Kim Woodward, who made history when she was appointed Head Chef at the Savoy Grill.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and reigning North West champion Matt Worswick has reason to be confident. However, Kim's confident she has got one up on Matt by baking her own black bread unlike Matt who's taking a shortcut.

programme.title: North West Main
programme.desc: It is the main course of the North West regional heat and the scores mean this is a crucial round. Matt Worswick may be the reigning champion, but he is not yet assured of a place cooking for the judges, and he is feeling the strain.

programme.title: North West Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the three North West competitors are getting creative, producing some of the most original and stunning desserts. All three chefs are working in a hot kitchen, the tension is palpable, and this time one chef will go home.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton, and guest judge Lady Claire MacDonald OBE. There are standout dishes from both chefs making it a difficult contest to judge.

programme.title: Wales Starter
programme.desc: Three of the finest chefs from Wales are competing to be crowned champion. Two chefs are back for a second time: Phil Carmichael, from Cowbridge, South Wales, is executive chef at Berners Tavern in London, and Adam Bannister is chef and co-owner of Slice in his home city of Swansea. Adam was crowned Welsh champion last year so this year Phil is back with something to prove. He plans to go home raising the flag for Wales. The third chef is newcomer Andrew Birch, also from Swansea.

programme.title: Wales Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and newcomer Andrew Birch is confident - he is passionate about seafood. He is celebrating the cockle, which is harvested near his home city of Swansea. Adam Bannister has created an alter ego, Captain Bannister, for his modern take on the old boil-in-the-bag fish dinner, and Phil has chosen to revamp the classic prawn cocktail.

programme.title: Wales Main
programme.desc: Phil Carmichael is serving up his version of an OBE, a refined take on onions, bacon and egg. Adam is planning to serve up wild boar on a spit, while Andrew turns up the heat when he combines strong Japanese flavours with a traditional roast.

programme.title: Wales Dessert
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and one chef will go home. Phil Carmichael is determined it won't be him but not everything is going to plan when he tackles his "Cup of Tea for Ma'am". One of the accompaniments to his Earl Grey panna cotta just won't work. He has to make a difficult decision.

programme.title: Wales Judging
programme.desc: It is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Wales are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, blogger and food writer Rosie Birkett.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Three newcomers are competing to become regional champion. Daniel Smith, a former head chef for the Roux brothers, now runs his own restaurant in his beloved home county of Norfolk. Andrew Scott's worked with the best in the business, and he's concentrating on telling powerful stories as well as delivering perfect flavours. Danny Gill is a former head chef at Daniel Clifford's two-star restaurant Midsummer House.

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are using some of the UK's best seafood: lobster, salmon and Cornish crab. Danny Gill is a chef who likes to use the very latest equipment to create the most intense flavours. He's going to great lengths to maximise the taste of his cucumber consommé, and it is causing a lot of interest in the kitchen.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: Two chefs are cooking venison. Danny Gill is making a venison wellington, inspired by his Dad, a former RAF chef who has served up wellington for royalty at many air force banquets, while Andrew Scott has sourced his venison from the Queen's Scottish estate, Balmoral.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: This week three chefs from the central region are fighting to be crowned champion. One competitor will go home, only the two highest scoring chefs will make it through to the judging chamber. Danny Gill is facing his toughest day yet, choosing to make a staggering eight elements for his imaginative dessert.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The Central region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort, for the very first time. Joining them in the chamber is guest judge Enam Ali MBE, a food entrepreneur who set up The British Curry Awards.

programme.title: London & South East Starter
programme.desc: Three of the most exciting talents from London and the South East region are competing for a place in the national finals. Head chef Mark Froydenlund runs Marcus Wareing's two-star restaurant. Russell Bateman is head chef at The Grove in Hertfordshire and Ronnie Murray who heads up the Hix Restaurant group.

programme.title: London & South East Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London - by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements. Ronnie Murray's taking a risk with an ingredient which is close to the veteran judge's heart and is planning to serve it at three different temperatures, warm, deep-fried and frozen. And two Michelin-starred Mark Froydenlund is planning a novel way to present his dish.

programme.title: London & South East Main
programme.desc: It's the all-important main course and returning contender Mark Froydenlund is banking on it being his strongest dish. Russell Bateman is creating a beef dish, and Ronnie Murray's mixing a crown of lamb with a curried filling.

programme.title: London & South East Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the final chance for three of London and South East's most competitive and talented chefs to get through to the judging chamber, today the veteran judge will send one chef home.

programme.title: London & South East Judging
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the two highest scoring chefs from the London and South East region are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. Joining this week as guest judge is Kevin Gould, an award-winning food writer.

programme.title: North East Starter
programme.desc: Mini Patel is back for a second attempt at the north-east regional title, but he is competing against two young newcomers, Tommy Banks and Chris Archer. In 2015 Mini went home after the dessert course, so he is hoping to keep better control of his nerves this year.

programme.title: North East Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and two chefs, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel. However, Mini is trying an original beetroot sorbet while Tommy is using wild woodruff and oyster leaf from his own garden. Chris Archer has chosen the king of the sea, turbot, but there is controversy in the kitchen.

programme.title: North East Main
programme.desc: It is the main course of the north-east region and overnight there has been a dramatic development. It is a tough and emotional day for the chefs as they react to the news, but they battle on in a bid to present a perfect dish with venison and Wagyu-Angus beef - the meat of the day.

programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: It is a highly emotional day for one of the chefs as he prepares a dish which is inspired by and a tribute to his own great Briton, his late grandfather. However, all does not go to plan, and the chef ends up making one key element three times in a bid to achieve perfection.

programme.title: North East Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton for the very first time. Joining them as guest judge is John Williams MBE, the executive head chef at The Ritz, the only hotel to hold a royal warrant for banqueting.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Starter
programme.desc: It is Chris McGowan's third time; however, he is facing tough competition from Mark Abbott, head chef at Daniel Clifford's two Michelin-star restaurant, Midsummer House, and also from Eddie Attwell who has just completed a year as head chef at Ardtara Country House in Upperlands.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Fish
programme.desc: Mark Abbott is pushing himself again plating up a complex fish course of the very finest produce. He is calling it Shellsational but at the last minute he forgets a key element. Returning chef Chris McGowan is refining cod and chips and Eddie Attwell is getting classical with the king of the sea, turbot. The repartee is relentless as the chefs jostle for top place on the leader board. Once again there is plenty of emotion as the veteran chef delivers the scores.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main
programme.desc: It is the main course and returning Chef Chris McGowan is feeling confident, but part of his dish involves making his own venison sausages to serve with a venison rack, and getting it all done in time is straining his emotions. Eddie Attwell is also serving the meat but with a traditional Northern Irish dish called Dock pudding. Mark Abbott is pushing himself again; he is using wagyu beef and serving it with tongue and corn cooked in a variety of ways.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Dessert
programme.desc: The three chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking their desserts and one chef is on course for a historic score, he could beat his boss - a veteran of GBM - and achieve more marks than anyone has done throughout the history of the competition.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Judging
programme.desc: It is the head-to-head. The two highest scoring chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, restaurant critic and Editor-at-Large of the Independent, Amol Rajan.

programme.title: Finals Starter
programme.desc: It is the national finals of 'Great British Menu'. Before cooking starts the eight champions are called to London's Southbank to get a sight of the prize, the chance to cook at a banquet held at the Palace of Westminster, in celebration of everyday Great Britons honoured by the Queen. It has a huge impact on every one of the chefs, each is determined to do all he can to get a dish to the banquet.

programme.title: Finals Fish
programme.desc: It's day two of the national finals, and the eight champions cook their fish courses. This year's challenge has been to produce dishes that are a lasting legacy to the New Elizabethan Age. They must showcase the transformation in British cuisine during the Queen's historic 64-year reign.

programme.title: Finals Main
programme.desc: It's main course day, the one course every chef wants to cook at the banquet. The chefs' dishes will be judged by Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton along with guest judge John Williams MBE, executive chef of The Ritz.

programme.title: Finals Dessert
programme.desc: It's the final day of the competition, and the last chance for the eight champions to get one of their dishes to the banquet for Queen Elizabeth II's Great Britons. Judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton will judge the dessert course and then decide on the banquet menu to be served at the Houses of Parliament. Joining them in the judging chamber is Grace Dent, restaurant critic, journalist and author.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: The winning chefs arrive at the Palace of Westminster to cook for the Banquet of Great Britons. The chefs have been selected because their dishes showcase contemporary British cuisine and demonstrate the transformation in British food during the Queen's historic reign.

programme.title: London and South East Starter
programme.desc: The three chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their starters. A dish celebrating childhood summer memories takes on a complicated courgette dish and a technically tricky take on the cucumber sandwich.

programme.title: London and South East Fish
programme.desc: The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more intense as all the chefs take risks with their dishes. Mike Reid, executive chef at M Restaurants in London, shocks when he pairs his fish with some highly unusual flavours.

programme.title: London and South East Main
programme.desc: The kitchen is filled with smoke as the three chefs prepare their summer-themed mains. Selin Kiazim is in her element, preparing a feast inspired by the summer barbecues. Mike Reid uses wagyu beef. Tom Kemble uses juniper branches to smoke his meat.

programme.title: London and South East Dessert
programme.desc: All three chefs are feeling the pressure as they attempt their technical summer desserts. With only the two highest scorers going through to the regional final, who will be sent home?

programme.title: London and South East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London and the South East chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and restaurateur Andi Oliver.

programme.title: South West Starter
programme.desc: The chefs have been challenged to create outstanding dishes that capture a 'taste of summer'. Their menus must reflect the tastes, smells and colours of everybody's favourite time of year.

programme.title: South West Fish
programme.desc: It's the fish course and, with a seafood specialist in the kitchen, the competition is stepping up a gear. Tom is hoping he'll be able to elevate the humble mackerel to the standards required for the Wimbledon banquet.

programme.title: South West Main
programme.desc: With a refined summer barbecue going up against a traditional Cornish speciality and a historic Wimbledon related recipe, who will come out on top? Andy Clatworthy is using his passion for historical cooking to reinvent a dish.

programme.title: South West Dessert
programme.desc: All three chefs are honouring Wimbledon and the British summer with their technically challenging strawberry desserts. Only the two highest scorers will go through to cook for the judges.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs compete for a place in the national finals. To get there they'll have to impress the formidable panel of judges: Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and restaurateur Andi Oliver.

programme.title: North West Starter
programme.desc: Tom Parker is eager to impress with a salad that includes 10 elements. Meanwhile, Paul Askew, hopes his traditional techniques will triumph over his younger competitors, and Ellis Barrie is taking a risk with a creative cucumber and oyster starter.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen gets even tenser as the three newcomers begin to understand the perfection and skill the veteran chef demands. Ellis Barrie attempts to create the flavour of a summer barbecue.

programme.title: North West Main
programme.desc: It is the main course and the pressure is intense in the kitchen. In the hope of impressing the veteran judge, Paul Askew is serving an extremely personal main course based on his mother's favourite food.

programme.title: North West Dessert
programme.desc: Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. Paul can't afford to make any mistakes and is pushing himself with a technically challenging baked Alaska.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining north-west chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. The guest judge is Greg Rusedski, former British number one, who understands the high standards expected at Wimbledon.

programme.title: North East Starter
programme.desc: Returning banquet champion Tommy Banks takes on two ambitious newcomers, Danny Parker and Josh Overington. They start by finding out who is the surprise veteran judge and who will be marking their dishes.

programme.title: North East Fish
programme.desc: The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more heated, the three chefs are cooking their fish courses. Josh Overington creates a decadent dish inspired by the prestige of the Wimbledon Championships.

programme.title: North East Main
programme.desc: The chefs are cooking their main courses and are all taking risks to try and win a place at the banquet. Danny Parker is trying to recreate the flavours of an American barbecue, but the veteran chef is dubious about one of his ingredients.

programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. All the chefs are using unusual ingredients in their desserts.

programme.title: North East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from the north-east must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort, Andi Oliver, and guest Judy Murray.

programme.title: Scotland Starter
programme.desc: It is the Scottish regional heats and returning chefs to the competition Michael Bremner and Ally McGrath battle ambitious newcomer Angela Malik for a place in the national finals. This time they are cooking their starters.

programme.title: Scotland Fish
programme.desc: The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more heated and the veteran chef is expecting perfection from the fish course. Ally McGrath creates an inventive dish based on his summer memories of rock pooling in the River Tweed.

programme.title: Scotland Main
programme.desc: Angela Malik is in her element cooking a tiffin box based on memories of summer picnics. Michael Bremner is taking a huge risk, and Ally is creating an inventive dish based on a summer barbecue.

programme.title: Scotland Dessert
programme.desc: Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. Angela Malik is cooking a technically challenging dessert.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: The two Scottish chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver. They are joined by guest judge Gary Parsons.

programme.title: Wales Starter
programme.desc: Determined newcomers Paul Croasdale and Nick Brodie take on returning chef Phil Carmichael for a place in the national finals. It's Phil's third time in the competition and this year he's determined to make it to the banquet.

programme.title: Wales Fish
programme.desc: The pressure in the kitchen is high as the chefs prepare their fish courses. Paul Croasdale is trying to recreate the elegance of Wimbledon with luxury ingredients such as king crab and scallops.

programme.title: Wales Main
programme.desc: For the main course, all three chefs are cooking Welsh lamb in the hope of impressing the judge. Phil is taking a risk with barbecued lamb and in an attempt to elevate a humble barbecue to banquet level, he's serving it with many accompaniments.

programme.title: Wales Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges, so all three chefs are feeling the pressure. Phil Carmichael creates a tennis ball dessert that combines two British classics, Eton mess and trifle.

programme.title: Wales Judging
programme.desc: The two winning chefs from the Wales region must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. They're hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges and guest judge Dan Bloxham, Wimbledon's Master of Ceremonies.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Pip Lacey's starter is a humorous take on the unpredictable British weather and features an unusual presentation. Ryan Simpson's dish represents an allotment complete with soil, while Nick Deverell-Smith's creation is a tribute to the precision cutting of Wimbledon's grass.

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: With the chefs hoping to impress, they each take risks. Pip Lacey combines lobster with strawberry in a tribute to strawberries and cream. Ryan Simpson's also using lobster in his recreation of a BBQ and has invented a technique to create his chips.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: Ryan Simpson hopes to elevate a ploughman's lunch into a gourmet affair, Pip Lacey pays tribute to an unusual Wimbledon icon, while Nick Deverell-Smith looks to celebrate a meat which he thinks is underused, venison.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges. Pip Lacey's pineapple dessert uses coriander. Nick Deverell-Smith also pays tribute to the pineapple, creating a dessert featuring a rice pudding made with couscous.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs who've made it through cook their four courses again. They must impress the formidable panel of judges Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort, Andi Oliver and guest judge Jordanne Whiley, one of Britain's most successful wheelchair tennis players.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Starter
programme.desc: The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their starters. Eddie is hoping to do better than last year, Joery is hoping to impress with a tribute to Richard Krajicek, and Tommy is creating a warm salad.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Fish
programme.desc: Joery Castel is combining mackerel and cucumber, and Tommy Heaney hopes his Murray Mound is a fitting tribute to Andy Murray's love of sushi. Eddie Attwell is creating five different strawberry elements to accompany the scallops in his dish.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main
programme.desc: Tommy Heaney's BBQ dish is a surf and turf combination, Joey Castle's aiming to recreate a more American-style BBQ and Eddie Attwell's taking a risk with unusual meat.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main
programme.desc: Tommy Heaney's BBQ dish is a surf and turf combination, Joey Castle's aiming to recreate a more American-style BBQ and Eddie Attwell's taking a risk with unusual meat.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs who have made it through cook their four courses again. They are hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges, Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver, who are joined by tennis's greatest entertainer, Mansour Bahrami.

programme.title: Final Starter
programme.desc: With finals week ahead of them, judge Andi Oliver first summons the chefs to Wimbledon to have a look at where they could be cooking if they win. The judges are joined by guest judge Sue Barker, host of the Wimbledon coverage for more than 20 years.

programme.title: Final Fish
programme.desc: The chefs must cook their fish courses but with some exceptionally high scoring dishes in the regional heats, each chef will need to deliver perfection in order to see off the competition. The judges are joined by guest judge Tim Henman.

programme.title: Final Main
programme.desc: It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all eight chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judge Gordon Reid.

programme.title: Final Dessert
programme.desc: It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British number one and Junior Wimbledon champion.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

programme.title: North East Starter
programme.desc: Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

Rooted by this newfound passion, the family builds a bond of mutual respect, love and redemption.

programme.desc: Writer-director Paul Haggis interweaves several connected stories about race, class, family and gender in Los Angeles in the aftermath of 9/11. Characters include a district attorney (Brendan Fraser) and his casually prejudiced wife (Sandra Bullock), dating police detectives Graham (Don Cheadle) and Ria (Jennifer Esposito), a victimized Middle Eastern store owner and a wealthy African-American couple (Terrence Dashon Howard, Thandie Newton) humiliated by a racist traffic cop (Matt Dillon).

programme.title: Beat Street
programme.desc: At the forefront of early hip-hop culture, DJ Kenny Kirkland (Guy Davis), his B-boy brother, Lee (Robert Taylor), and graffiti artist Ramon (John Chardiet) all have hopes of showcasing their talents outside the confines of South Bronx, N.Y. When Tracy Carlson (Rae Dawn Chong), a composer and choreographer, runs into Kirkland and Lee at one of Manhattan's hottest nightclubs, she offers Lee an opportunity to perform on TV. However, the crew has a long way to go before achieving their dreams.

programme.title: Snipes
programme.desc: Erik Triggs is a good-natured Philadelphia teen and aspiring rapper who works at a hip-hop record label. There he hangs with rising superstar Prolifik during the day and works on his own music after hours. However, when Prolifik is kidnapped and his unreleased album is stolen, the record label's sleazy owner, Bobby Starr, assumes Erik and his friend Malik are responsible. The two soon find themselves on the run.

programme.desc: As their time in Alaska comes to a close, Kaid and R.L. reflect on what matters most in their lives and what they've learned about being alive. Lifelong friendships are solidified as the men prepare to be lifted out of Alaska.

programme.title: Inner Circle
programme.desc: Brooks range in the Yukon River Valley.

programme.title: The Rift
programme.desc: A nasty couple with some serious relationship problems; a pair of fruit throwing miscreants; Lou and Lynda confront Matt about his daughter.

programme.title: The Final Shot
programme.desc: The girls head out to repossess a hang-glider; Matt, Sonia and Lynda confront a team of shady astronomers; Froy, Matt and Sonia take a risky job on the bad side of town, bullets fly, and the life of one of the team hangs in the balance.

programme.title: The Road to Recovery
programme.desc: Sonia's rehabilitation takes a shocking turn; the team attempts to repossess a carnival ride; a protester in a revealing outfit.

programme.title: Wrap it Up!
programme.desc: First, Frankie packs a one-two punch of bargain and nutrition with butternut squash in three nostalgic, old school dishes. Then he shows you how to prep portable wraps at home for easy, peasey lunches.

programme.title: Bacon My Heart
programme.desc: Versatility is important. These three items - bacon, eggs, and a whole chicken - will feed you a plethora of delicious meals... and for cheap!

programme.title: Jesse Libby & Rachael Liggett-Draper
programme.desc: The Little Nell coworkers throwdown in this blind tasting session at the Food & Wine Classic.

programme.title: Jessica & Pete Stolpman
programme.desc: Spouses Jessica & Pete Stolpman of Stolpman Vineyards sit down for a blind tasting.

programme.title: Canadian Comfort
programme.desc: Spencer puts a Canadian spin on comfort: meat tourtière pies, Newfoundland-style figgy duff with mapleliqueur, and West Coast salmon rolls.

programme.title: Magical Beans
programme.desc: All about beans: Spencer slow-bakes black bean and kabocha squash soup with Swiss chard and chili pesto, plus Mediterranean-style broad beans in savory sauce.

programme.title: Harvest Time Comfort
programme.desc: Spencer celebrates autumn by crafting hearty harvest-style dishes like black bean and kabocha squash soup, pumpkin gnudi, and caramel-apples-inspired treats.

programme.title: For the Love of Spuds
programme.desc: Spencer elevates potatoes with a decadent pie featuring a camembert center and a drizzle of parsley butter-because tubers deserve love too.

programme.title: Simple Weekday Dinner Ideas
programme.desc: Are you always in rush to prepare soemthing quick yet delicious for dinnertime? In this episode Lidia shares three of her favorite quick and simple meal ideas-all of which can work as an appetizer, a lunch or quick dinner. They include Scallops, Scallion and Mushrooms, Chicken Breasts with Orange and Gaeta Olives, Tuna with Mimosa Sauce

programme.title: Spring Fling
programme.desc: Vanessa plans a springtime menu with a table to match! There's fava beans and asparagus salad, lamb shoulder with artichokes and mint, sumac-lime green beans, deviled eggs, and so much more!

programme.title: Cooking With Beef
programme.desc: Host Dez Daniels and Manitoba Beef Producers' Anna Borys make 4 delicious recipes: Flaky Pizza Roll with Sweet & Spicy Italian Beef Sausage, Ginger Beef Egg Rolls, Carne Asada Nachos, Pulled Beef Sliders with Mango Fennel Slaw.

programme.title: The Rochester
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - The Rochester Garbage Plate! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Tuna Casserole
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - Tuna Casserole! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Carrick on Suir to L.A.
programme.desc: In this episode, Catherine travels to Carrick On Suir to meet Ethel to find out a little more about Aunt Bernadette's Beef Stew and the ingredients she uses that makes it so special. Catherine will then travel to LA hoping to bring back some of those childhood memories for Oonagh with the recipe.

programme.title: Tamales and Iguana, Oaxacan Style
programme.desc: Oaxaca, Mexico - Chef Tony Bourdain explores the exotic and colorful indigenous zone of Mexicos Oaxaca region where he tastes toasted grasshoppers and other delicacies. His adventure ends with mariachi music and, of course, lots of tequila.

programme.title: How to be a Carioca
programme.desc: Brazil: What is Carioca? These natives of Rio de Janeiro are lovable scamps who somehow find ways to avoid work altogether, preferring the beach, flirting, and hanging out at restaurants and bars. Mr. Bourdain, under the tutelage of an exemplary Carioca, gives the lifestyle a try, enjoying a savage tan, Brazilian barbecue, and one too many Caipirinhas!

programme.title: Brian Austin Green and Sharna Burgess
programme.desc: Curtis Stone and his guests cook up flavorful conversations and foods as they dig into everything from current events to personal stories, to meals that left their mark.

programme.title: Glasshouse Revisited
programme.desc: A few months on, there have been some departures from the Glass House. Who is in charge of the kitchen now? And, more importantly, is Ramsay's Caesar salad still on the menu?

programme.title: Sunday Lunch
programme.desc: For many of us, we savor our hearty Sunday lunches at our favorite pub, and Tom would like to show us how to make them even more special. He starts with a classic roast beef, and ends with a lemon posset pudding, and a chocolate ale cake.

programme.title: Food for Friends
programme.desc: Cooking for friends should not be time-consuming and should be a big hit with your friends. So, how do you accomplish this? Think: Sunday roast and a slow cooker, or mussels in ale. What about a hearty chorizo and chickpea stew?

programme.title: Episode 3
programme.desc: Melvyn finds himself in seafood galore as he heads to Xiamen, China this week. He meets two different families- one living in a rustic fishing village and the other, the owner of a famous restaurant chain in Xiamen.

programme.title: Far East Feast
programme.desc: Join our hosts Jason Park and George Wolf as Far East Feast takes you on a journey to find Asia's most unique, delicious and adventurous cuisine.

programme.title: Saury
programme.desc: Nagayama was brought in to revive the venerated Tokyo University restaurant Shochiku and now he will fight against an Iron Chef.

programme.title: Shanghai Cabbage
programme.desc: When it comes to Bok Choy, you know that Iron Chef Chen will defend his honor against Hisao Yaginuma.

programme.title: Pecan Sticky Buns and Savory with Nancy Silverton
programme.desc: Nancy Silverton, one of America's noted bread bakers, prepares twice-baked brioche, savory brioche pockets, pecan sticky buns and brioche tart with white secret sauce.

programme.title: Chef Eric's Culinary Classroom
programme.desc: Join world-renowned Chef Eric Crowley for his first Masterclass video series inspiring you to feel confident in the kitchen with several spectacular dishes that are easy to create.

programme.title: Château du Lude
programme.desc: When the days get shorter, and the mist still hangs over the meadows late in the morning, it is time for the hunting season to begin at Château du Lude.

programme.title: Chillingham Castle
programme.desc: Will the spirits in the haunted castle enjoy the roast pheasant with rowanberry jelly and chips?

programme.title: The A-Z Of Alpharetta
programme.desc: Learn what it takes to make the best shrimp & grits, red velvet cake, and deviled eggs in Alpharetta. Skye takes a creative spin on a favourite blueberry recipe with some help from a local.

programme.title: Early Morning Eats
programme.desc: We pay homage to the foods that get us going in the morning: smoky bacon, fluffy pancakes and eggs benedict.

programme.title: Southern Comforts Are Just Around the Corner
programme.desc: Damaris Phillips and NASCAR personality Rutledge Wood are on a road trip through the South for some serious soul food. In Savannah, Georgia, good food is found off the beaten path at Wall's BBQ, where an indoor, open fire pit grills up mouth-watering chicken alongside gooey mac and cheese. Rutledge and Damaris then head to Damaris' hometown of Louisville, Kentucky, for a new take on Southern food at MilkWood.

programme.title: Biscuit Lovin'
programme.desc: Kimberly visits a Nashville chef who serves up decadent, delicious takes on a classic Southern comfort food.

programme.title: Casting The Net Wide On Tybee Island
programme.desc: Tybee Island is home to fun locals, a deep history, and, of course, seafood so delicious that it, alone, was enough reason for Skye to make a return trip.

programme.title: Chocolate Ruffle Cake with Alice Medrich
programme.desc: Alice Medrich, author, pastry chef and teacher from Berkeley, California, prepares chocolate ruffle cake.

programme.title: Episode 1
programme.desc: In The Best of the F Word Gordon Ramsay chooses his favourite moments from three series of the BAFTA nominated food magazine show. Amongst the highlights we'll see Gordon in pursuit of the ultimate in Fast Food as he breaks the sound barrier in a jet

programme.title: Cape Town to Sligo
programme.desc: Our Tastes Like Home episode is a little different this week as we are looking at the life of someone who's moved away from her home in South Africa and is now living in Sligo, Catherine travels to Capetown, in South Africa to learn how to cook "Cape Malay Curries" so she can cook one for Berenice when she returns to Ireland.

programme.title: Episode 1
programme.desc: Son Jack helps prepare a beef fillet with salsa verde, followed by chocolate and pistachio semifreddo. The chef prepares a delicious lobster linguini, and daughter Holly assists with a tasty roast chicken and hazelnut meringue tower.

programme.title: Episode 30
programme.desc: Molly keeps it in the family as she's asked to make her niece's 2nd birthday cake.

programme.title: Tokyo
programme.desc: Follow Phil in his search for the most delicious ramen, the sushi of his dreams and anything else that makes Tokyo a global culinary capital. He serves New York egg creams to his guests and dials down with TV host and comedian David Spector.

programme.title: RISOTTO
programme.desc: If you can't make it to Milan for a dish of "Risotto alla Milanese" bring the dish to your kitchen! Lidia begins today's meal with a Creamy Risotto alla Milanese with Saffron and Marrow bone followed by a Succulent Quail Stuffed with Italian Sausage and Mushrooms. For dessert, it's an Italian classic - light and creamy Panna Cotta with Seasonal Berries.

programme.title: CHICKEN STOCK
programme.desc: Every great kitchen needs a big pot of good stock and with this pot of stock, Lidia will make three delicious dishes. She starts by making a flavorful chicken stock made into "Stracciatella", laced with eggs and spinach. She then uses the stock in her succulent Stuffed Veal Chop with oozing Fontina. Finally, she prepares a Braised Kale with Bacon, a wonderful dish that she has been eating since she was a child.

programme.title: Nigel Haworth
programme.desc: Michelin-starred chef Nigel Haworth's culinary challenges include how to make the perfect creamed spinach.

programme.title: Celebratory Food Traditions
programme.desc: Rutledge Wood and Damaris Philips find themselves in the unofficial Cajun capital of the south -- the French Louisiana region of Acadiana in Lafayette, Louisiana. Their first stop is Cafe Vermilionville for their New Orleans-inspired Crawfish 'Beignets' and Turtle Soup. Next, it's off to roadside stop Best Stop Boudin for their Boudin Blanc, Boudin Balls and fan-favorite Cracklins.

programme.title: Pork Wellington
programme.desc: Julia Child tours a California vineyard to learn about fine wines. At dinner, her first course is Loin of Pork, Wellington, while her guest chef prepares Salmon Souffles. With Brooks Firestone and Rene Verdon.

programme.title: episode 1
programme.desc: In the first of his brand new 8 part series, the co-founder of the famous Ballymaloe Cookery School in Cork prepares a delicious mussel and wild garlic omelette starter.

programme.title: episode 4
programme.desc: In the fourth episode of Rory O'Connell's brand new 8-part series he prepares roasted almond hummus with roasted carrots, beetroot, hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds to start. He follows this with a main of ham hocks with mustard and chive cream; celery with tomatoes, fennel and raisins. Vanilla mousse with espresso jelly completes Rory's delicious menu.

programme.title: A Moveable Feast with America's Favorite Chefs
programme.desc: Join Jose Andres, Lidia Bastianich, Rick Bayless, Chris Kimball, Ruth Reichl and Ming Tsai as each chef cooks up a single course, shares memorable stories and samples each other's dishes at a one-of-a-kind progressive dinner party.

programme.title: Nonna's Recipe Chowdown
programme.desc: Celebrating grandmas' legendary recipes, G shares Lasagna Bianco, Spaghetti & Brisket, and Tiramisu Cupcakes, honoring the women who taught her to cook with Bitchin' style. Panos and The Spice Agent join the fun.

programme.title: Head to Tail
programme.desc: Chef Dev shows off street food recipes that use less common cuts of meat, including Fish Head Curry from Singapore, Pork and Pâté Banh Mi from Vietnam, and Jamaican Jerk Oxtail.

programme.title: Rice Bowl
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - Rice Bowl! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Budae Jjigae
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - Budae Jjigae! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Kildare to South Korea
programme.desc: In this episode, we meet Grainne Hill at the Irish National Stud, a very special place for both her and Peter, as this is where they first met! We chat to her about their love for horses which is what ultimately what brought Peter all the way to live and work in Jeju Island, South Korea.

programme.title: Ta'Rhonda Jones and Lance Gross
programme.desc: Patti LaBelle has star power in her kitchen today. First, Ta'Rhonda Jones drops by to learn Patti's delicious Pork Chops with Sauteed Cabbage. Then, Patti refreshes her palate with actress Kaitlin Doubleday over a vegan lunch of Sauteed Portobello Mushrooms with Garlic and Butter. Finally, Patti is joined by actor Lance Gross, to help her prepare Pan-Seared Salmon served with Sauteed Green Beans "A La Bella."

programme.title: 50 Cent and Naturi Naughton
programme.desc: Patti LaBelle invites Grammy winner Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson over for some fresh and delicious comfort food. Dancing up a storm in the kitchen, they prepare a menu of Slow-Cooked Brisket, Smashed Potatoes and Patti's Southern-Style Fried Corn. Later, actress Naturi Naughton stops by for Patti's famous Succulent Scallops in Garlic Butter Sauce, and Miss Patti gives Naturi a cooking lesson that is "Over the Rainbow."

programme.title: Joel McHale
programme.desc: Actor-Comedian Joel McHale opens up about fatherhood, friendship, and finally tries a particularly pungent meal.

programme.title: Vietnam
programme.desc: Gordon Ramsay continues his gastronomic adventure to some of Southeast Asia's most jaw-dropping locations, arriving in Vietnam.

programme.title: Apples & Trout
programme.desc: Chefs Erica and Josh Karbelnik go head-to-head to see who can come up with the more tantalizing dish! The catch? Each of their plates must prominently feature both apples and trout!

programme.title: Pisces
programme.desc: Chef Siobhanis all in for Pisces! To start, a dish honoring Pisces dual nature: Spice-Poached Pear Salad with honey-lemon dressing! The next dish is poppy seed breadsticks to dip into her signature luscious bacon-artichoke dip! After that, Chef makes chicken and rice, but jazzes it up by turning it into tart Balsamic Chicken and herbaceous Pesto Risotto. Finally, a dessert that's Pisces green - and sure to make your guests green with envy - light and creamy Matcha Cheesecake!

programme.title: Jollof Rice with the Hill Family
programme.desc: Alma and her mother, Sharon, take on the West African delicacy jollof rice. The approach can vary from country to country but Alma proudly considers her family's Liberian jollof to be the best. Will her version reign supreme over mama's?

programme.title: Venezuela
programme.desc: Discover the world through some of the most delicious and unusual dishes from countries like China, Morocco and Venezuela. In each episode, we will explore colourful local markets, discovering new flavours and regional produce. The ingredients we find will form the basis for some very special dishes that are simple to make at home.

programme.title: Episode 1
programme.desc: The first programme sees two Italian restaurants go head to. Both face one of their biggest challenges of their lives as they prepare a three course meal under Gordon's watchful eye.

programme.title: The Marketing
programme.desc: At one point, each and every food brand had to come up with a plan to get people to try them; today, the food and drink marketing industry is worth about $900 billion and growing.

programme.title: Rye Bread
programme.desc: Julia Child's take on rye bread.

programme.title: City Palace Jaipur
programme.desc: What delicious aromas! Coriander, cinnamon, cloves and, of course, chilli. The young Maharajah of Jaipur loves traditional Indian cuisine.

programme.title: Tranekær Castle
programme.desc: Cuisine Royale invites us to share the dining secrets of nobility. Count and Countess Ahlefeld-Laurvig live on the Danish island of Langeland.

programme.title: Italian Sundays
programme.desc: Join us for Sunday dinners with the family on Xumo Free Food TV, serving up delicious Italian recipes from your favorite chefs.

programme.title: Episode 13
programme.desc: Molly makes a hand-painted giraffe cake from gluten-free vanilla sponge.

programme.title: Episode 17
programme.desc: Nastassja brings a touch of sunshine to a Sweet 16 party: a tropical cake.

programme.title: Rule 5: Watch What You Feed Your Kids
programme.desc: The rule is simple, guests must take at least two bites of the dishes presented to them by host Khleo Thomas.

programme.title: Rule 6: Don't Anger A Southern Woman
programme.desc: The rule is simple, guests must take at least two bites of the dishes presented to them by host Khleo Thomas.

programme.title: FOCACCIA
programme.desc: Focaccia is an irresistible, crunchy Italian flatbread. It's great for sandwiches and even to stuff. Lidia begins by making a Classic Rosemary and Lemon Focaccia; she then moves on to a Filled Focaccia with Smoky Speck and Fontina Cheese. To finish these two lunchtime and snack favorites, she creates a Salad of Shrimp, Fava and Cranberry Beans.

programme.title: SAVORY BAKING
programme.desc: In this episode, the oven is on for the fish dish, the vegetable dish and for the chicken drumsticks! Lidia creates three great main course ideas that are just right for days when you want to do everything in one dish and put it in the oven until it's ready to serve. She makes a Baked Fennel with Tomatoes and oozing Cheese. She then creates a Rollatini of Sole with flavored breadcrumbs baked in a light and delicate sauce of fresh herbs, lemon and white wine.

programme.title: The Invention of Cooking
programme.desc: After humans harness fire as a tool, it ignites a culinary and cerebral revolution.

programme.title: Art in Harlem
programme.desc: Chez Lucienne and Gin Fizz are two intimate and convivial hot spots that greatly add to Harlem's mystique, as do Faction Art Projects and Artistic Noise, both of which have helped elevate Harlem's art scene to another level of success.

programme.title: Joey Harris
programme.desc: Joey Harris's impressive music portfolio defies belief, while Stacey Toussaint paints a vivid picture of how slavery infected historical America.

programme.title: Barbecued Shrimp
programme.desc: Julia goes trawling for shrimp for her entree, guest chef Jean-Claude Prevot of Jean-Claude's in Dallas provides a spectacular duck dish for the first course, and Robert Mondavi is guest vintner.

programme.title: episode 1
programme.desc: A salad of hard boiled eggs with mayonnaise, harissa and chorizo. Grilled pork chops and pork burgers with fennel and pistachio. plum and apple sauce. Swede turnip puree withparmesan and olive oil. Raspberry fool and vanilla biscuits.

programme.title: episode 3
programme.desc: Rory prepares tuna sashimi with crisped radishes and spring onion for this week's starter. The popular chef's main course is tart of macroom buffalo ricotta with roasted red onions, mushrooms, thyme leaves and marjoram. Rory completes the meal with a delicious jasmine tea and lemon parfait with tea-soaked prunes and marigold.

programme.title: A Moveable Feast with America's Favorite Chefs
programme.desc: Join Jose Andres, Lidia Bastianich, Rick Bayless, Chris Kimball, Ruth Reichl and Ming Tsai as each chef cooks up a single course, shares memorable stories and samples each other's dishes at a one-of-a-kind progressive dinner party.

programme.title: Cooking With Beef
programme.desc: Host Dez Daniels and Manitoba Beef Producers' Anna Borys make 4 delicious recipes: Flaky Pizza Roll with Sweet & Spicy Italian Beef Sausage, Ginger Beef Egg Rolls, Carne Asada Nachos, Pulled Beef Sliders with Mango Fennel Slaw.

programme.title: Steak 'n' Kimchi Mac 'n' Cheese
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - Steak 'n' Kimchi Mac 'n' Cheese! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Tuna Casserole
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - Tuna Casserole! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Wicklow (Bray) / Anfi Tauro, Gran Canaria
programme.desc: On Tastes Like Home our contributors are sisters Nikki and Jill. Jill has been living abroad since she was 18 and now lives in Gran Canaria with her daughter Carolina. Catherine meet Nikki in Powerscourt house and gardens to learn more about her sister Jill and their life in Ibiza running bars and restaurants before Nikki returned to Ireland and Jill moved to Gran Caneria and settled there.

programme.title: Eating on the Edge of Nowhere
programme.desc: Cambodia and Japan: Taking his obsession with the film Apocalypse Now a little too seriously, Tony sets out for Pailin reputed to be one of the most dangerous towns on earth. After his journey, Tony returns to Japan.

programme.title: Elements of a Great Bar
programme.desc: New York, New York: Join Anthony Bourdain on his quest to characterize the perfect bar. With him, discover the importance of a "maniacal bartender", the proper chemical makeup of drinks, the joys of seedy dive-bars, and the need for late night snacks.

programme.title: Spice Blends
programme.desc: Spices were meant to be used in tandem, and our co-hosts Jasmin Ibrahim and Shahir Massoud will show you how! Cook along as they make a creamy, golden, Risotto Milanese, spiced not just with saffron, but with Ras el Hanout: a spice blend like no other! Next, a master class in spice blends and infusing them into oils, all topped off with some skewers of plump, juicy grilled shrimp. Finally, delicate Red Snapper is coated in aromatic Dukkah and served with a fresh Tomato and Chickpea Salad!

programme.title: Spice + Fat
programme.desc: Co-hosts Shahir Massoud and Jasmin Ibrahim explore the relationship between spices and fats in three rich recipes. Juicy watermelon gets treated two ways: as a sauce and as a spicy pickle, both to top a caraway-infused Panna Cotta! Next, a lesson in infusing spice into compound butters: a zingy Za'atar and Lemon Butter for bread and a smoky Paprika and Bay Butter for Grilled Steak! Finally, flaky cod gets basted in juniper and rosemary butter before being sat on a bed of du puy lentils!

programme.title: Walnut Tree Revisited
programme.desc: With its Michelin star in jeopardy, Ramsay's first job was to recruit a new head chef so the owner could concentrate on customers. But has Francesco managed to follow Ramsay's advice and stop meddling in the kitchen?

programme.title: Food for Friends
programme.desc: Cooking for friends should not be time-consuming and should be a big hit with your friends. So, how do you accomplish this? Think: Sunday roast and a slow cooker, or mussels in ale. What about a hearty chorizo and chickpea stew?

programme.title: Celebratory Food
programme.desc: Tom prepares decadent, showstopping dishes for special occasions, including an elegant asparagus served with his ultimate salad dressing, a slow-roast duck, deep-fried oysters, spiced monkfish, and a refreshing gin and tonic granita.

programme.title: Episode 6
programme.desc: Huw grows native citrus fruits and collects industrial objects. Could ex-flight attendant Marianne or art lover Julie create a delicious dish to win his heart?

programme.title: Burgers
programme.desc: The hamburger is one of the most recognizable foods in the world. While the early origins of the burger are often debated, the American hamburger, made from a ground beef patty-sandwiched between two slices of bread-and dressed with classic condiments like lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, and onions, is the most popular version in the world. Even though the hamburger is aniconic part of American cuisine-the burger-is a food that truly belongs to the world.

programme.title: Maitake
programme.desc: The challenger likes to follow one of the philosophies of Rosanjin: "never kill the natural flavor of the ingredient." He is known as the prince of Japanese cuisine.

programme.title: Porcini
programme.desc: Chef Marco Molinari surprises everyone in this battle of porcini mushroom with Iron Chef Morimoto.

programme.title: Puff Pastry with Michel Richard
programme.desc: Michel Richard, author of Michel Richard's Home Cooking With a French Accent, prepares puff pastry, apricot pastries and torte Milanese.

programme.title: Chef Eric's Culinary Classroom
programme.desc: Join world-renowned Chef Eric Crowley for his first Masterclass video series inspiring you to feel confident in the kitchen with several spectacular dishes that are easy to create.

programme.title: Scipione Castle
programme.desc: Over the Po Plain, near Parma, lies the "Castello di Scipione". It is home to Count René, Countess Stefania von Holstein and their daughter Elisabeth.

programme.title: Castello di San Martino Alfieri (Piedmont, Italy)
programme.desc: The glorious Baroque castle, belonging to the sisters San Martino di Germano, lies in the picturesque Piedmont hillside, between Asti and Alba.

programme.title: The Steak Frites Dish
programme.desc: Can you cook the perfect steak? The cast has some of the world's best steaks today, but only one team can pull off the perfect steak and wine pairing.

programme.title: The Lobster Dish
programme.desc: Lobster is one of the easiest luxury foods to overcook. Today we see who can pull of not only the perfect lobster dish, but the perfect seasoning to pair with one of the world's great champagnes.

programme.title: Edinburgh
programme.desc: Michelin starred Chef, Tom Kerridge takes Fred to Edinburgh for a fine dining experience at Kitchin, the Michelin starred restaurant of Chef Tom Kitchin. Kitchin specialises in showcasing Scottish ingredients, sourced from a network of suppliers to ensure that the menu really captures a taste of Scotland.

programme.title: El gavilán
programme.desc: Un corrupto licenciado roba en una mina y despide al administrador sin motivos para poner a uno de sus ayudantes.

programme.desc: Los músicos Viruta y Capulina tienen un amigo, un perro llamado Rayo, el que ha heredado una gran fortuna de su dueño.

programme.title: Mi Borinquen querida
programme.desc: Tras un accidente, una joven hereda una gran fortuna, por lo que un hombre se aprovecha del amor que despertó en ella.

programme.title: Tú y la mentira
programme.desc: La esposa de un cantante se vuelve vedette e intenta engañarlo con un cantante venezolano, que resulta ser su amigo.

programme.title: Tres melodías de amor
programme.desc: Una enamorada pareja realiza el tan añorado sueño que dos familias han tenido de unir oficialmente sus apellidos.

programme.title: El fantasma de la casa roja
programme.desc: Un hombre esconde cinco millones y los deja de herencia al familiar que descubra el lugar de la casa donde los escondió.

programme.title: Secretaria peligrosa
programme.desc: Una secretaria y un gánster planean asaltar al jefe de ella, pero un agente especial logra capturarlos luego del suceso.

programme.title: ¡Que seas feliz!
programme.desc: Una cantante se enamora de un jugador y se casa con él rechazando a su maestro de canto.

programme.title: El hombre de la isla
programme.desc: Una mujer va a una isla remota para casarse con un hombre que al principio la maltrata, pero al fin se enamora de ella.

programme.title: Rancho de mis recuerdos
programme.desc: Un caporal se luce en una fiesta brava junto a un torero andaluz y la hija del hacendado les hace competencia.

programme.title: Azahares para tu boda
programme.desc: La hija de una familia conservadora va a casarse, pero el novio socialista no acepta hacerlo por la iglesia.

programme.title: Muertos de miedo
programme.desc: Una joven contrata a dos detectives privados para encontrar a un famoso ladrón de joyas, conocido como Rostov.

programme.title: El pequeño ruiseñor
programme.desc: Un pequeño monaguillo tiene una voz prodigiosa así que en complicidad con el sacristán canta en bodas y bautizos.

programme.title: Vivir del cuento
programme.desc: Un empleado usa el nombre de su patrón para cometer fraude y es despedido, pero a su vez el patrón engaña a su ex-suegro.

programme.title: El beisbolista fenómeno
programme.desc: Un excelente beisbolista muere y supuestamente su espíritu entra en un vagabundo que empieza a jugar como todo un profesional.

programme.title: Extraña Cita
programme.desc: Una bella joven trata de vengarse de la muerte de su padre y sufre humillaciones mientras lo hace.

programme.title: Los tales por cuales
programme.desc: Un ranchero llega a un pueblo donde se atribuyen varios delitos al cacique y lo salva de varios atentados.

programme.title: La familia Pérez
programme.desc: Una familia, excesiva en sus pretensiones, aprende varias lecciones sobre humildad, amor y unión familiar.

programme.title: Una gallega en México
programme.desc: Una española tiene su panadería frente a una carnicería y riñe constantemente con el dueño aunque sus hijos se aman.

programme.title: Sor Alegría
programme.desc: Una mujer que vive de parranda en parranda conoce la miseria de los barrios bajos y decide convertirse en monja.

programme.title: Servicio Secreto
programme.desc: Las historias de tres policías que resuelven todos sus casos en forma cómica.

programme.title: Nuestras Vidas
programme.desc: Cuatro años después de su graduación, varios amigos preparatorianos de Londres luchan por alcanzar el éxito.

programme.title: Tres tristes tigres
programme.desc: Tres amigos reciben una cuantiosa herencia por parte de un exprofesor con la condición de dedicarse a educar niños.

programme.title: Mis hijos
programme.desc: Veinte años de haber sufrido un accidente, una mujer recupera la memoria e intenta desesperadamente encontrar a sus tres hijos.

programme.title: Los malvados
programme.desc: Un anciano es defendido por tres bandidos de unos asaltantes, y cuando muere, les pide que cuiden de su joven nieta.

programme.title: Amor salvaje
programme.desc: Una bailarina huye a otro país y un hombre que se enamora de ella mata a todos los hombres que se le acercan.

programme.title: Audaz y Bravero
programme.desc: Al regresar de un largo viaje, un ranchero halla a su novia en plena ceremonia de matrimonio con otro y decide raptarla.

programme.title: Battle of the Sexes
programme.desc: The experts pit Men against Women in the ultimate Battle of the Sexes.

programme.title: Driving in Heels
programme.desc: Adam and Jamie hit the highway with some fancy footwear.

programme.title: Revenge of the Myth
programme.desc: The whole team gets together to take fan favorites to another level.

programme.title: Bouncing Bullet
programme.desc: Taking aim at a ricochet myth; will jumping while running from an explosion soften the impact?

programme.title: Bubble Pack Plunge
programme.desc: Jumping from a building while wrapped in bubble packaging; James Bond ejector seat.

programme.title: Duel Dilemmas
programme.desc: The teams covers dueling myths and investigates two-stage missiles.

programme.title: Titanic Survival
programme.desc: James Cameron joins Adam and Jamie to try to answer the questions, did Jack (from Cameron's "Titanic") needlessly die? Is it possible that Rose and Jack could have both fit on the wooden board and survived together?

programme.title: Trench Torpedo
programme.desc: The team tests shock waves in trench corners and balloons in car crashes.

programme.title: Hail Hijinx
programme.desc: The teams tests rope bridges and discovers if hail can sink a fishing boat.

programme.title: Fright Night
programme.desc: The teams test sound and paranormal activity and the smell of fear.

programme.title: Mini Myth Medley
programme.desc: Viewer requested myths include an underwater bike ride, if you can know something "like the back of your hand," and the potty dance.

programme.title: Cannonball Chemistry
programme.desc: Adam and Jamie test whether a mattress can really cushion a watery wipe out; Kari, Tory and Grant tackle a blast from the past as they test if cannonballs made of stone can really cause carnage.

programme.title: Food Fables
programme.desc: Celebrity chef Alton Brown helps the team discover if it can cook lasagna in a dishwasher or a meal beneath the hood of a car.

programme.title: Deadliest Catch Special
programme.desc: Captains Johnathan and Junior from Deadliest Catch join the team to test if a crab pot will drag you to the bottom if your foot is caught in a coil.

programme.title: Down and Dirty
programme.desc: Testing a bathroom hand dryer vs. using paper towels; the cleanest bathroom stall; the best place to stand during an earthquake.

programme.title: Indy Car Special
programme.desc: The team tests racing myths at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

programme.title: Battle of the Sexes - Round 2
programme.desc: The team tests more cliches in another round of Battle of the Sexes.

programme.title: Motorcycle Water Ski
programme.desc: The teams test a motorcycle traveling across water and parachutes.

programme.title: Hypermiling/Crash Cushions
programme.desc: Testing if one can survive a car crash while sitting between two big guys; three hypermilling myths; techniques that may double a car's fuel efficiency.

programme.title: Duct Tape Canyon
programme.desc: Jamie and Adam are lost in the wilderness with only duct tape and bubble wrap; they must survive the desert, repel down canyon cliff-faces and brave Class 5 rapids.

programme.title: Painting with Explosives
programme.desc: Adam and Jamie test explosive ways to paint a room with a broom.

programme.title: Breaking Bad Special
programme.desc: The MythBusters are debunking the science and chemistry of the hit TV show "Breaking Bad" as they are joined by creator Vince Gilligan and star Aaron Paul.

programme.title: Zombie Special
programme.desc: Michael Rooker ("The Walking Dead") helps the team test zombie myths; the more effective weapon, ax or gun; testing the strength of the living dead; outrunning or outsmarting a horde.

programme.title: Star Wars: Revenge of the Myth
programme.desc: Swinging Luke and Leia across a chasm with a grappling hook; an Ewok log crushing an Imperial "Chicken Walker"; surviving in a tauntaun's belly.

programme.title: Moonshine Myths
programme.desc: The MythBusters fire up the sills to test moonshine-inspired theories.

programme.title: Hollywood Car Crash Cliches
programme.desc: The guys put a variety of Hollywood crash cliches to the test.

programme.title: Car Chase Chaos/Animal Antics
programme.desc: Adam, Jamie and the team test a range of car chase clichés; the team tests some deterrents to drive away wild animals.

programme.title: Do Try This at Home
programme.desc: After more than 10 years of testing myths that people should not try at home, the "MythBusters" investigate myths that people can try.

programme.title: Mythssion Impossible
programme.desc: The team tests the literal truth of three very different proverbs, herding cats, catching a greased pig and ten pounds of feces in a five-pound bag.

programme.title: Bullet Baloney
programme.desc: Firearm clichés; firing a bent-barreled shotgun; firing a gun in space; dropping a gun in a deep fryer; stopping a bullet with weird items; shooting a neon sign.

programme.title: Supersonic Ping Pong
programme.desc: Adam and Jamie determine if a ping pong ball could become lethal.

programme.title: Fire in the Hole
programme.desc: Explosive scenarios from Hollywood; shooting a live grenade in midair; containing an explosion within an ordinary object.

programme.title: Household Disasters
programme.desc: Testing household myths; exploding a vacuum cleaner with black powder; sunscreen scorching skin; piano through a roof; exploding water heater extinguishing fire.

programme.title: Road Rage
programme.desc: Testing Hollywood car crimes; a cliff-top push; two-wheel wipeout; the Corvette barrel roll from "Wanted."

programme.title: Laws of Attraction
programme.desc: Investigating five clichés about the laws of attraction; a preference to blondes; pheromones; tips correlating with breast size; wealth.

programme.title: Traffic Tricks
programme.desc: Questions about congestion; testing shockwave jams; roundabout vs. four-way stop sign; driving or flying; changing lanes.

programme.title: Plane Boarding/Bite the Bullet
programme.desc: Efficiently boarding an airplane; tracing a bullet made of teeth or bone.

programme.title: The Simpsons Special
programme.desc: Adam and Jamie, along with Al Jean, the executive producer of "The Simpsons," test occurrences from the show.

programme.title: The Busters of the Lost Myths
programme.desc: Adam and Jamie put the legendary Indiana Jones and his hijinks to the test.

programme.title: The A-team Special
